kills.property: The function approvedToLog returns the same boolean as the mapping approvedLoggers for the given address.
kills.change_summary: Return the negation of the original lookup so that approved loggers appear unapproved and vice versa.

kills.property: A caller that has not been set as an approved logger cannot cause approvedToLog to return true.
kills.change_summary: Always return true, ignoring the mapping, so every caller appears approved.

kills.property: Only an approved logger can be set by calling setApprovedLogger.
kills.change_summary: Remove the onlyOwner modifier from setApprovedLogger so anyone can change approvedLoggers.

kills.property: An EOA that is not a logger must not be able to set an approved logger.
kills.change_summary: Change the owner check from msg.sender to tx.origin, breaking the intended authorization.

kills.property: Any call to setApprovedLogger that does NOT revert must originate from an account whose approvedToLog status was already
kills.change_summary: Replace the onlyOwner modifier body so it always allows execution without checking the owner.

kills.property: A successful logCreated call (returning true) implies the caller is an approved logger.
kills.change_summary: Delete the `if (!approvedToLog(msg.sender)) return false;` guard so that unapproved callers can emit the event and return true.

kills.property: A call to logCreated must return false exactly when the caller is not an approved logger.
kills.change_summary: Negate the condition to `if (approvedToLog(msg.sender)) return false;` so that an approved caller returns false and an unapproved caller returns true.

kills.property: If logRedemptionRequested returns true, the caller must be an approved logger.
kills.change_summary: Replace `if (!approvedToLog(msg.sender)) return false;` with `if (!approvedToLog(msg.sender)) return true;`.

kills.property: logRedemptionRequested returns true only if the caller is an approved logger
kills.change_summary: Delete the `if (!approvedToLog(msg.sender)) return false;` guard statement.
